dct_description_sm: Large furbearers, such as the wolverine, the wolf, and the grizzly bear, constitute one of the least known components of the tundra ecosystem, yet they play a considerable role in structuring the abundance of other Arctic species and bear a very important significance for Nunavut communities. Inuit hunters, by experience, hold extensive libraries of observations about the furbearers, although their knowledge on their ecology can be limited due to the elusive nature of these predators. Scientists are also very limited in their understanding of the large carnivores and very few studies have been conducted on this topic in Nunavut. In this NGMP project, we have built an innovative research framework involving Inuit communities, Government of Nunavut biologists and researchers from the Universit du Qubec  Rimouski, to study the large furbearers on a large-scale perspective. The key piece of our approach was the implementation of a monitoring program to collect the carcasses of animals harvested by local hunters. Hunters received cash compensation for their contribution to the program. The program was run across 13 communities during a minimum of 3 years (hunting seasons 2010-11 to 2012-13). We collected many samples on the carcasses to determine the age, sex, health, and the diet of the large furbearers. Diet was determined looking at the animals stomach content and through molecular analyses (stable isotopes). Our program became a live-platform for the sharing of observations, stories, and knowledge between the local communities, the local conservation officers (who were actually collecting and storing the carcasses) and our team of researchers. We ran hunters surveys, formal interviews and mapping sessions with hunters/trappers and elders in order to document local observations and knowledge. Our main researcher, Dominique Berteaux, and Ph.D. student, Vincent L'Hrault, have spent prolonged periods of time with Inuit families in Kugluktuk, Arviat, Rankin Inlet, and Baker Lake, participating in many informal traditional activities and hunting trips to learn more about the large furbearers and the Inuit culture overall.

dct_title_s: Ecological monitoring of large terrestrial carnivores (wolverines, wolves and grizzly bears) in Nunavut, 2010-2013 (NGMP ID EC10)
